mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by 2% or more year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 4.5% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE stays below 4.5% for four months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise of at least 1% in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) within the same month signals a broad-based expansion in economic activity, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO and HOUST both rise by at least 1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both INDPRO and HOUST rise by at least 1% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls by >0.5% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS declines by more than 0.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual shock of inflation and policy tightening, which increases uncertainty and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS both exceed their 12-month averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS exceed their 12-month averages in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) acceleration above 0.5% after three months of deceleration signals a recovery in labor market momentum, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth accelerates above 0.5% after three months of deceleration
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive after PAYEMS growth accelerates above 0.5% following three months of deceleration.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth rate (GDPC1) below 1% for four consecutive quarters signals economic stagnation, which depresses earnings and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 remains below 1% annualized for four consecutive quarters.
